raw: {"open_points":[{"subject":"sandbox scratch-limit outcome","kind":"contradictory observability","text":"“the runner ignores the signal the host sends for a write past it, so the write fails with an error the code can see” conflicts with “a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`”: if agent code catches the write error and returns conforming output, the parent has no stated indication that the scratch limit was hit.","question":"How does `sandbox` learn that the per-file scratch limit was hit when agent code catches the resulting error, and must that execution still be `resource_exhausted`?","options":["Record every over-limit write through a runner mechanism and return `resource_exhausted` even when caught","Treat a caught write error as ordinary code behavior and allow success when the returned output conforms","Classify only an uncaught over-limit write, under a separately specified outcome"],"default_guess":"Record the hit inside the runner and return `resource_exhausted` even when the code catches the write error.","unit":"sandbox"}]}

set_aside.subject: sandbox scratch-limit outcome
set_aside.text: “the runner ignores the signal the host sends for a write past it, so the write fails with an error the code can see” conflicts with “a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`”: if agent code catches the write error and returns conforming output, the parent has no stated indication that the scratch limit was hit.
set_aside.question: How does `sandbox` learn that the per-file scratch limit was hit when agent code catches the resulting error, and must that execution still be `resource_exhausted`?
options: Record every over-limit write through a runner mechanism and return `resource_exhausted` even when caught
Treat a caught write error as ordinary code behavior and allow success when the returned output conforms
Classify only an uncaught over-limit write, under a separately specified outcome
set_aside.default_guess: Record the hit inside the runner and return `resource_exhausted` even when the code catches the write error.
